newsitem.title: UK: BT, Sky in TV venture - report.
newsitem.headline: BT, Sky in TV venture - report.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc, BSkyB Plc, HSBC's Midland Bank and Matsushita are forming a 500 million stg UK venture to supply decoders for digital television, the Sunday Telegraph said.

The newspaper quoted industry sources as saying that BT and satellite broadcaster Sky, whose main shareholder is Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd , would each take 30 percent with the other partners each taking approximately 20 percent.

A British Telecomm spokesman said digital TV was an area the company was interested in given the convergence of telecommunications and broadcasting, but said the company could not comment on the details of the report.
"We are talking to a lot of companies all the time and don't comment on speculation," he said.

The report said the plans had been submitted to the Department of Trade and Industry and to telecommunications watchdog Oftel, and the parties had pledged that they would offer third-party access to the decoder boxes, which could offer more than 200 TV channels as well as on-line services.
The newspaper said the partners had held talks with other electronic manufacturers, including Samsung, Pace and Philips, to ensure enough decoders were built to supply the British market.
It said the partners would inject cash into the venture and subsidise sales of the boxes to speed the introduction of digital TV, with the decoders available by next Christmas.
No comment was immediately available from BSkyB.
